terra.problem: 1 Samuel 17:15 says David went back and forth from Saul to tend the sheep; it does not say Saul was in a palace.
Papa says he gave a neighbor an oven mitt, but he lives alone on his cookie planet. The backstory does not establish a neighbor he could have given it to.
The passage says the people and Saul's officers were pleased. It does not say Saul's own feelings changed from being pleased.
The joke invites the baker to picture Saul singing the song, inventing a reaction for a Bible person and making him the target of the joke.
Calling this a 'proud dad moment' suggests Saul is David's father. David is not yet Saul's son-in-law either.
'There was no stopping' goes beyond the text's statement that Saul kept a jealous eye on David from that day forward.
Papa comments on how he is telling the passage when he says he is not going to joke about it.
The text says David eluded Saul twice. It does not say David got away from the spear both times.
The passage says David eluded Saul; it does not say he walked away.
The comparison does not track: a batch taken out of the oven cannot 'come back' flat. The joke's action does not make sense.
'He knew where he was going' adds a detail about David that the passage does not state.
Battle talk does not first come after David's answer. Saul has already told David to fight the LORD's battles in verse 17.
The drawer comment does not explain why Papa respects David's answer, and the connection comes across as a non sequitur.
'David just saw a chance' asserts and limits David's thoughts. The text says he was pleased to become the king's son-in-law.
The passage does not say David gave a verbal yes or that he did not hesitate.
The joke compares the killing of two hundred Philistines to doing a favor, making the violence itself the comic material.
'The harder Saul tried, the more he saw it' adds a progression and connection that the text does not state.
The passage says Saul was David's enemy; it does not say whether a peace treaty was signed.
Saul is not described as glaring, and David's being more successful than Saul's officers does not establish that he won every battle.
Papa refers to being forgotten without identifying the drawer, leaving bakers who do not know his backstory without the context.
David's name being highly esteemed does not establish that everybody knew it.
